title: Damped look-at tracker with yaw and pitch limits
purpose: Turn turrets, heads, eyes, cameras and spotlights toward a moving target the way mechanisms do: yaw and pitch around a rest orientation, clamped to limits, approached with exponential smoothing and a hard cap on the angle turned per second. Deterministic, frame-rate aware and free of three.js dependencies.

engine.name: node
engine.notes: Pure ES2020, also runs in any browser; applyTo writes a three.js object's quaternion through quaternion.set. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run.

exports.name: LookAtTracker
exports.signature: new LookAtTracker(options = {}, restQuaternion = [0, 0, 0, 1]); update(position, target, deltaSeconds) -> {yaw, pitch, quaternion, clamped}; quaternion; applyTo(object); yaw; pitch
exports.summary: A tracker with its own yaw and pitch that turns toward the clamped aim each update.

exports.name: aimAngles
exports.summary: The unclamped aim: yaw about the rest +Y toward +X, pitch toward +Y, for the rest +Z axis.

exports.name: clampAim
exports.summary: The aim clamped to the yaw and pitch limits.

exports.name: orientationFromAngles
exports.signature: orientationFromAngles(restQuaternion, yaw, pitch) -> [x, y, z, w]
exports.summary: Rest, then yaw about +Y, then pitch about +X.

exports.name: stepAngles
exports.summary: One smoothed, speed-capped update toward the goal.

options.name: maxSpeed
options.meaning: Cap on |yaw step| + |pitch step| per second, which bounds the angle actually turned.

options.name: smoothing
options.meaning: Time constant of the exponential approach; 0 jumps as far as the speed cap allows.

options.name: yawLimit
options.meaning: Largest yaw either side of rest; pi means unlimited, turning the shorter way round.

limits: A kinematic rule, not a motor model: no inertia, torque or overshoot, and the speed cap bounds the turn per update, not angular acceleration. Yaw and pitch form a gimbal, so a target straight along the rest up axis has no defined yaw and the yaw holds where it was. Position, target and rest orientation must share one frame (usually the object's parent); applyTo writes the local quaternion and assumes that. The tracked axis is the object's +Z, as three.js Object3D.lookAt uses for non-cameras; a camera needs a rest turned half a turn about Y. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Yaw-pitch gimbal decomposition of a look direction in a rest frame
Exponential smoothing with a frame-rate independent factor 1 - exp(-dt / tau)
Rotation-angle bound by the L1 norm of gimbal angle steps (triangle inequality on SO(3))
